brief: How to protect 4 hours of deep work in a calendar full of meetings.

slots.headline: How to Protect Four Hours of Deep Work Daily

slots.title: Audit Your Calendar
slots.body: Scan your week for low-priority meetings that steal focus. Cancel or delegate anything that doesn't require your direct input. Reclaiming these slots is the first step toward protected deep work.

slots.title: Block Deep Work
slots.body: Treat your deep-work block like an immovable client meeting. Place it on your calendar at the same time each day. Consistency trains colleagues to respect your focus hours.

slots.title: Set Clear Boundaries
slots.body: Share your focus hours with your team so expectations are clear. Turn on do-not-disturb and close email during these blocks. Boundaries only work when you enforce them visibly.

slots.title: Batch Meetings Together
slots.body: Cluster calls into one or two afternoons rather than scattering them. Batching preserves longer uninterrupted stretches for demanding projects. Your brain switches gears less often, saving mental energy.

slots.title: Default to Async
slots.body: Replace status meetings with brief written updates or recorded videos. Async communication keeps everyone informed without real-time disruption. Reserve live meetings for decisions that genuinely require discussion.

slots.title: Protect Your Energy
slots.body: Schedule deep work during your peak cognitive hours, usually mornings. Avoid back-to-back meetings before your focus block. Guarding this time is how you produce your best work.
